Given edge_ne_zero, the clause `edgeSegment P i ∩ edgeSegment P (i+1) = {P (i+1)}` holds iff the two consecutive edges are not antiparallel (non-collinear: only the shared endpoint; positively collinear: only the shared endpoint; antiparallel: overlap of positive length). Hence edge_ne_zero + consecutive ⟺ Regular (RegularLocus.lean:12, regular_iff_edges :18-19), and remote_disjoint covers every other pair of edge indices (two distinct indices are consecutive or remote; for n = 3 every pair is adjacent and consecutive covers all three pairs). So Embedded ⟺ traversal injective mod n ⟺ simple closed polygonal curve; flat vertices (turn 0) allowed as sm-3:4791 requires; Embedded ⟹ Regular (leaf Embedded.regular, statement line 175). n ≥ 3 is printed at def:polygon (sm-1:28). NOT REFUTED. I tried each of the requested attack lines against SM.cb_embedded_rotation (statement file work/reviews/cb-embedded-rotation-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt, S:30-33 Embedded, S:40-41 IsSupportingVertex, S:44-58 EmbeddedRotationData, S:476-477 theorem; kernel-confirmed identical to the built module via #check/#print) and none yields a blocking discrepancy.

1. "Embedded" admitting a non-simple polygon or excluding a printed one — FAILS. For n >= 3 every pair of distinct edge indices is either adjacent (j-i in {-1,0,1}, Polygon.lean:63-64) or remote (Polygon.lean:66); remote closed segments are disjoint (S:32) and consecutive ones meet exactly in the shared vertex (S:33), with all edges nonzero (S:31). Consequences I checked by hand: all vertices distinct (P i = P(i+1) would give a zero edge; remote vertices lie on disjoint segments); no vertex lies on a non-incident edge (for n >= 4 index i+2 is remote from i, for n = 3 the consecutive clause forces it; P(i-1) in E_i would force P(i-1) = P i); doubled-back pairs and collinear degenerate triangles are excluded (E_i and E_{i+1} would share a segment, not a singleton); a doubly traversed polygon is excluded (E_0 = E_3 remote, not disjoint). So Embedded P is exactly "the traversal circle is injective with nonzero edges", i.e. the simple closed polygonal curve. Flat vertices are admitted (positively collinear consecutive edges still meet only in P(i+1)), as sm-3:4791 requires. The source never defines "embedded" formally (informal uses sm-1:479 "embedded dart" with a reflex vertex, sm-1:489, sm-3:772 "no crossings ... embedded oriented circles"); the consumer's "uniform and embedded (m_Q=0)" (sm-3:4803) is reached by the bridge leaf embedded_of_generic_of_isEmpty_crossing (S:207-209). No constructible counterexample polygon exists on either side.

2. Regular / pm_one — exact. Regular P (RegularLocus.lean:12-13 with RegularPair u v := u ≠ 0 ∧ v ≠ 0 ∧ ¬∃ r<0, v = r•u) is def:regular verbatim (sm-1:386-396). rotationNumber P = (Σ principalTurn)/(2π) (RotationNumber.lean:10) is lem:rot's rot(P) (sm-1:408); principalTurn P i = arg(conj(ℓ_{i-1})·ℓ_i) whose imaginary part is det(ℓ_{i-1},ℓ_i), so sign ϑ_i = sign det as printed (sm-1:391). Kernel check /tmp/er_check2.lean: principalAngle (1,0) (0,1) = π/2, i.e. a left turn is positive. pm_one (S:46) is "rotation +1 or −1" literally. Regular is redundant given Embedded (S:175) but is the printed word (FR-ER-3): harmless.

3. Sign clause (FR-ER-2) — weaker than printed? NO, equivalent modulo an elementary fact, and non-vacuous. (a) IsSupportingVertex demands N ≠ 0 (S:41), so the clause cannot be triggered vacuously at every vertex. (b) Local geometry: at a supporting vertex the whole polygon lies in {⟪N,x−P i⟫ ≥ 0}; if the turn is a left turn (det(e_{i−1},e_i) > 0) the sector on the traversal's left is {α e_i − β e_{i−1} : α,β ≥ 0}, and ⟪N, α e_i − β e_{i−1}⟫ = α⟪N,e_i⟫ − β⟪N,e_{i−1}⟫ ≥ 0, so −N is NOT in the left sector; hence the open −N half-plane (which contains no point of the polygon and lies in the unbounded complement) is on the traversal's RIGHT and the bounded side is on the LEFT. So "left turn at a supporting vertex → rot = +1" is precisely the printed proof's own convention "Traverse the boundary with this disc on the left ... rotation 1 ... The opposite traversal negates every turn and gives −1" (sm-3:4790-4798). Note the printed STATEMENT (4762-4764) does not even say which orientation gives +1; only the proof fixes it, and the Lean fixes it the same way. (c) exists_supporting (S:58) is a proved theorem (axioms of cb_embedded_rotation = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no sorryAx), so the orientation field is non-vacuous: a supporting vertex with nonzero turn exists. (d) IsSupportingVertex also admits vertices in the relative interior of a hull edge; the clause is still true there (the half-plane argument above does not use extremality, and the theorem is proved), so this is a strengthening, not a weakening. (e) Kernel checks on the source's own dart P = ((2,1),(2,4),(0,0),(4,0)) (sm-1:479; /tmp/er_check3.lean, /tmp/er_check4.lean): the reflex base vertex 0 is NOT supporting for any N (so the clause cannot misfire at a reflex vertex whose turn sign disagrees with rot), while hull vertex 2 = (0,0) IS supporting for N = (1,1) and has det > 0 (left turn), consistent with rot = +1. The only unformalized content is "the left local sector belongs to the bounded complementary region", which is exactly the Jordan content of deferred row 57; since the statement is forbidden to depend on row 57 and the source has no definition of the region, the local rendering is the only admissible one, and the sole consumer (sm-3:4811) uses |r| = 1.

4. Hidden hypotheses — none. [NeZero n] (S:476) follows from hn : 3 ≤ n and is needed only for Fintype (ZMod n) in rotationNumber; n ≥ 3 is printed in def:polygon (sm-1:28); LabelledTuple n instead of Polygon n is licensed by sm-1:54-61, and Embedded/IsSupportingVertex/rotationNumber are shift-invariant (S:199-200, S:427-428, RotationTheorem.lean:24 last clause).

5. Dependence on lem:gauss-two-discs (D-ER1) — none. #print axioms SM.cb_embedded_rotation = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; the theorem type mentions only Regular, Embedded, EmbeddedRotationData; the lemma is named only in the header prose (S:1). sm-3:428-436 is cited only by the printed proof (4766), not the printed statement.

6. Reviewer discrepancies — all re-examined, all genuinely non-blocking: extra field exists_supporting (true, disclosed §1.6/FR-ER-7, needed for determinacy); orientation quantified over all supporting vertices (true strengthening); Regular and [NeZero n] redundancies; labelled representative. No reviewer discrepancy is real-and-blocking.
